name: Redwire Corporation

profile.description: Redwire is a space and defense technology company building space infrastructure, including solar arrays, in-space manufacturing, deployable structures, sensors and autonomous systems. Q2 2026 revenue was $117.1M (up 89.6% YoY) with record contracted backlog of $542.1M, and FY2026 revenue guidance is $450-$500M [1].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Redwire expanded from space infrastructure into defense tech with the Edge Autonomy acquisition, opening a new revenue stream with defense backlog of $138.4M at Q1 2026 [1]. AI Deployment (1/2): The company cites digital engineering and AI automation, but no quantified savings or AI revenue were found [2]. Market Share (1/2): A meaningful niche player in space solar arrays and in-space systems, but not a category leader with cited share data. Pipeline (1/2): Programs are named across civil, national security and commercial space, but timelines and revenue visibility are limited. R&D (0/1): No peer-relative R&D intensity evidence found.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Redwire's stated goal of building the future of aerospace infrastructure is clear and mission-driven but not yet validated over decades [2]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinct charitable programs found. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor reviews cite fragmented leadership and high turnover, though 84% approve of the CEO [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): Net insider selling dominates, with AE Industrial entities selling millions of shares and over $229M in sales in three months [3].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically as a Growth stock; PEG unavailable and excluded (8 weight units). D/E of 5.5% (1.0), revenue growth of 89.6% YoY (1.0) and a 5-yr revenue CAGR above 10% (1.0, 2x weight) score maximum, but ROE of -18.2% (0, 2x weight), a negative forward P/E (0) and a -57.3% profit margin (0) score zero [1]. Weighted sum 4.0 of 8 gives 5. Daily dollar volume of about $161M passes the liquidity floor.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Space hardware, launch-adjacent infrastructure and defense platforms are physical, government-contracted systems that AI cannot replace, and AI automation is more likely to benefit programs than threaten them [2]. No analyst warnings on AI disruption were found. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantified AI revenue is disclosed.

infinite_game.summary: Redwire has a plausible space-infrastructure purpose and has pivoted into defense, but it is a roll-up reliant on acquisitions, with executive turnover, thin margins and heavy sponsor selling. The cause is real but not yet proven across cycles.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Enabling humans to build and operate in space gives Redwire a distinctive, big cause that shapes its portfolio, though the company is only a few years into public life [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Glassdoor reviews cite terrible HR, fragmented leadership and high turnover, and the company is described as an aerospace roll-up [2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of framing competitors as teachers; competitive language is not documented.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Adding defense tech through acquisition broadens the model but is incremental rather than abandoning a core business [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Investing through operating losses to build backlog to $542.1M and entering defense shows long-term commitment, but the pattern is not yet multi-decade [1].

investment_thesis: Redwire at $10.88 has a $2.7B market cap and is delivering hypergrowth: Q2 2026 revenue was $117.1M (up 89.6% YoY), Q1 gross margin expanded to 26.6% from 14.7%, and contracted backlog reached a record $542.1M, 4.6x quarterly revenue [1]. FY2026 guidance of $450-$500M implies about 41.6% growth at the midpoint, with demand from civil, defense and commercial space [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that the profit margin is -57.3%, ROE is -18.2%, and the stock has run about 223% year to date before Jefferies downgraded it to Hold, saying upside is limited until backlog converts to revenue [3]. AE Industrial has sold tens of millions of shares, with insiders net selling, creating an overhang, and Glassdoor shows turnover and HR complaints [2][3].
key_catalysts: Conversion of the record $542.1M backlog into revenue to reach FY2026 guidance of $450-$500M [1]
Gross margin expansion, already from 14.7% to 26.6% year over year in Q1 2026, moving toward profitability [1]
Defense tech growth from the $138.4M defense backlog and national security space demand [1]
key_risks: Insider and sponsor selling overhang: AE Industrial entities sold over $229M in three months and Jefferies cites limited upside after a 223% rally [3]
Persistent losses with a -57.3% profit margin and negative forward earnings, so valuation rests on execution [1]
Integration and turnover risk from the roll-up structure, with reviews citing fragmented leadership [2]

backlog.note: Record contracted backlog of $542.1M at Q2 2026 (+64.5% YoY); Q1 2026 split was space $359.7M and defense tech $138.4M. Funded share and TTM book-to-bill not disclosed in sources reviewed; green on record-backlog criterion.
